summary: M3 Wiring & Exposure — register 5 dormant evaluators, wire WritingStyle 8D to backend, resolve M2 deferrals, add graph write operations, expose foreshadowing lifecycle + character depth + consistency dashboard, wire narrative analysis endpoints
approach: Three-phase wiring strategy. Phase 1 establishes shared infrastructure (evaluator registration, structured score transport, style integration, M2 deferrals). Phase 2 builds on Phase 1 with graph write operations and high-value feature exposure (foreshadowing lifecycle, consistency dashboard, character depth). Phase 3 is independent stretch (narrative pattern analysis). All features follow the same pattern: backend module → MCP endpoint → frontend API function → UI component.

stages.input: Dormant evaluator classes, WritingStyle 8D types, M2 deferred items
stages.output: 10 registered evaluators with per-module scores, structured style transport, resolved deferrals

stages.input: Phase 1 score transport, GraphManager read ops, ForeshadowingManager, CharacterManager
stages.output: Graph write ops with validation, foreshadowing lifecycle endpoints + UI, per-module consistency dashboard, character depth UI

design_decisions.reason: Phase 1 establishes shared infrastructure that Phase 2 features consume. Phase 3 is independent stretch.
Existing 3-score UI must continue working. Structured per-module scores are additive, not replacing.

design_decisions.decision: Graph engine write ops as shared infrastructure module
design_decisions.reason: Single validation layer, consistent behavior, avoids duplication across F2 and F6.
Established pattern in graph.js/critic.js works. No new abstractions.

patterns: MCP endpoint pattern: import { jsonResponse, parseBody } from '../utils.js'; async handler returning jsonResponse(result)
Graph scope resolution: resolveGraphScope(body) → { workspaceId, projectId }
Frontend API pattern: async function → invoke MCP endpoint → return typed result
Evaluator pattern: BaseEvaluator subclass with name/description/relatedSkill getters + evaluate() method
conventions: No new external dependencies — use existing React, Zustand, TailwindCSS, Tauri stack
Backward compatibility — never break existing 3-score evaluation UI
Follow coding philosophy: simplicity, existing patterns, no premature abstractions
dependencies: TASK-005 depends on TASK-004 (graph write ops needed for foreshadowing persistence)
TASK-006 depends on TASK-001 (per-module scores from evaluator expansion)
TASK-007 depends on TASK-004 (graph write ops needed for character depth storage)
